Name: e_fold_cv
Title: E-Fold Cross-Validation for Model Performance Estimation
Experiment: Develop an alternative to k-fold cross-validation named e-fold cross-validation. Instead of a static k it uses an intelligently chosen or dynamically adjusted paramter e to optimize the number of folds and to minimize computational energy while maintaining reliable model performance estimates.

Name: adaptive_lr_sgd
Title: Adaptive Learning Rate Techniques for SGD in Matrix Factorization
Experiment: Explore adaptive learning rate strategies, such as learning rate schedules or techniques like AdaGrad and RMSprop, to enhance the efficiency of SGD during matrix factorization, aiming for faster convergence and reduced energy consumption.

Name: sparsity_regularization
Title: Sparsity-Inducing Regularization for Energy-Efficient Matrix Factorization
Experiment: Introduce sparsity-inducing regularization techniques such as L1 regularization in the `update_parameters` function to enforce sparsity in the latent factors. Start with L1 regularization and compare the performance with the baseline model. If feasible, implement and test more advanced techniques like group lasso. Evaluate the impact on model performance (RMSE, MAE) and computational efficiency (training time, memory usage). Compare the results with the baseline model to assess any trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

Name: adaptive_early_stopping
Title: Adaptive Early Stopping for Energy-Efficient Matrix Factorization
Experiment: Enhance the early stopping mechanism by incorporating an adaptive approach that considers the rate of change in validation loss over multiple epochs. Modify the `sgd` function to include this adaptive early stopping criterion. Specifically, implement a moving average of the validation loss improvement over a window of epochs (e.g., 5 epochs), and stop training if this average improvement falls below a predefined threshold (e.g., 0.001). Compare the energy efficiency and accuracy metrics (RMSE, MAE) with the baseline early stopping method.

Name: svd_initialization
Title: Low-Rank SVD Initialization for Energy-Efficient Matrix Factorization
Experiment: Modify the `main` function to include an initial low-rank approximation of the user-item interaction matrix using truncated Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) with `scipy.sparse.linalg.svds`. Use the resulting matrices to initialize the user and item latent factors before performing stochastic gradient descent (SGD). Ensure the integration is seamless by matching the dimensions of the SVD matrices with the expected latent factor dimensions. Compare the energy efficiency and model performance (RMSE, MAE) with the baseline model that uses random initialization for the latent factors. Evaluate energy efficiency improvements by measuring training time and computational resource usage.

Name: parallel_sgd
Title: Hybrid Parallelism for Energy-Efficient Matrix Factorization
Experiment: Implement hybrid parallelism (data and model parallelism) in the `sgd` and `update_parameters` functions using parallel processing libraries like `joblib` or `multiprocessing`. Distribute the workload of updating user and item latent factors across multiple cores. Apply parallelism to the loops within the `update_parameters` function and the validation loop in the `validation_loss` function. Profile the code before and after parallelism implementation to identify bottlenecks and measure performance gains. Measure the impact on training time, computational energy usage using time and power monitoring tools, and model performance (RMSE, MAE). Compare the results with the baseline model to assess improvements in energy efficiency and accuracy.

Name: quantized_matrix_factorization
Title: Quantized Matrix Factorization for Energy-Efficient Recommender Systems
Experiment: Modify the `update_parameters` function to incorporate quantization of the latent factors and biases immediately after each parameter update during the SGD process. Implement different quantization levels (e.g., 8-bit, 16-bit) and compare their impact on model performance (RMSE, MAE) and energy efficiency (training time, memory usage). Specifically, after each update to bias_user, bias_item, factors_user, and factors_item, apply the specified quantization level. Evaluate the trade-offs between accuracy and energy efficiency by conducting experiments with varying quantization levels and comparing the results with the baseline model.
